affected_condition: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in Cyrus SASL. The add_to_challenge() function in the DIGEST-MD5 plugin computes the size of the buffer needed for a challenge/response field before DIGEST-MD5 quoting is applied, but does not recompute that size when quoting (escaping special characters) makes the value longer. The under-sized buffer is then passed to strcat(), causing a heap-based out-of-bounds write whose size depends on attacker-controlled input. A malicious or on-path DIGEST-MD5 (or HTTP Digest) server can trigger this flaw in a connecting client by supplying a crafted challenge field, such as realm or nonce, most likely resulting in a crash of the client application.
reason: Trigger requires the Cyrus DIGEST-MD5 add_to_challenge mechanism. Exact image SASL plugin directory contains only sasldb, with no DIGEST-MD5 plugin. Supported app uses managed Npgsql SCRAM and OAuth, not Cyrus SASL; fixed curl plain-HTTP healthcheck supplies no authentication credentials or negotiation options. Cyrus core is present transitively through LDAP, so the package is not declared absent.
limitations: Exact unmodified reference API image and compose configuration.
No custom credential caches/keytabs, KRB5 environment, Negotiate handlers, LDAP clients, RTMP clients, SASL modules or modified curl configuration.

Exact image has no krb5kdc/kadmind/kadmin/kpasswd, KDB plugins or gssrpc/kadm5 libraries. Application authenticates with Identity cookies/OAuth, not a Kerberos acceptor or administration service. Npgsql default Prefer may load GSS to seek credentials, but default initiator acquisition fails with no credential handle in this image; supplied reference compose does not supply a cache/keytab. No supported caller exposes the described server/admin endpoint.
limitations: Exact unmodified reference API image and compose configuration.
No custom credential caches/keytabs, KRB5 environment, Negotiate handlers, LDAP clients, RTMP clients, SASL modules or modified curl configuration.
Libraries remain installed and may be loaded; this is an affected-call-path exclusion, not library repair.
Npgsql10 Prefer does attempt default GSS credential discovery; never classify this as GSS library absent or never loaded.
Kerberos-enabled custom database endpoints or operator credential injection require reassessment.

affected_condition: librtmp (RTMPDump) through 2.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in AMFProp_Decode that reads an AMF0 strict-array element count before checking that four bytes remain. A malicious RTMP server or man in the middle can send an AMF0 body ending with a strict-array type byte and fewer than four trailing bytes to crash the client.
reason: Trigger requires parsing an RTMP/AMF strict array from an RTMP server. librtmp is installed and transitively loaded by curl, but the only supported curl invocation uses fixed http://api:8080/health/ready with no redirect-following. Provider/OAuth calls are HTTP(S) SocketsHttpHandler; no supported caller speaks RTMP or invokes AMFProp_Decode.
limitations: Exact unmodified reference API image and compose configuration.
No custom credential caches/keytabs, KRB5 environment, Negotiate handlers, LDAP clients, RTMP clients, SASL modules or modified curl configuration.
Libraries remain installed and may be loaded; this is an affected-call-path exclusion, not library repair.
